note: The highest-traffic primitive in the codebase, and the one whose CSS is SCOPED and injected — so `.manager-chip.svelte-<hash>` lands UNLAYERED while `styles/fabricate.css` imports at `layer(modules)`. That is why the tone story is worth looking at rather than reading: a caller's own rule cannot be assumed to reach this chip, and an editor header is a 34px button beside a ~20px pill for exactly that reason.

states.hover: No prop; see the plinth's pseudo-class readout. A `span` chip has no hover treatment at all — only `tag="button"` gives it one, and then from the caller's own class.
states.focus-visible: No prop. It is focusable only as `tag="button"`; tab to it on the plinth after switching the host.
states.disabled: No prop. `tone="disabled"` is a COLOUR FAMILY and not a state — the sheet joins it to the WARNING ramp — so it paints amber and sets no attribute, and nothing announces the chip as unavailable. A `tag="button"` chip can take a real `disabled` through the rest spread, which is the caller's to spell.
states.loading: No prop. A chip states a fact that is already resolved; there is nothing for it to await.
states.invalid: Not applicable: a chip carries a reading, never an entry that could be rejected.
states.readonly: Not applicable: a `span` chip is read-only by construction, which is what a mark is.
states.empty: Not applicable: it renders one mark, never a collection. Clearing `children` renders an empty pill, which is a missing reading rather than an empty state.

unknobbed.why: An EXTRA class appended to the primitive's own. It is how a caller reaches layout context from the global sheet — `manager-editor-tab-badge` positions a badge inside a tab button — and those rules sit at a higher specificity than this scoped block. Driving it would let the lab paint a chip the design system does not draw.

A `bind:this` handle on the rendered node, because `bind:this` on a COMPONENT yields the instance rather than the element. `SearchablePopover` needs it to measure its chip-shaped trigger and to restore focus to it. The lab hands props DOWN, so binding it here would give the node two owners.

Every other attribute — `title`, `aria-label`, `role`, `data-*` hooks, `onclick`, `type`, `disabled` — is forwarded onto the rendered element. The set is open and its members are either a caller's own selector or only meaningful once `tag="button"` has changed what the chip is, which is already driven.
